## [2026-09-11 23:50] Dashboard tick: keep — `/journal` Real change log (Move #6.x live-data integration + cross-page intelligence)

- **Branch:** dashboard-improver / 2026-09-11
- **Status:** keep
- **Reason:** PASSES improvement metric on 3 axes: (1) **live-data integration** — the new `<GitChangeLog />` panel on `/journal` renders the actual `git log` output for the dashboard subtree, captured at build time by an extended `parseGitLog()` step in `dashboard/scripts/parse-content.mjs`; (2) **cross-page intelligence** — git history is now queryable through the same filter chips + search box + copy-as-markdown pattern as `<JournalSearch />`, so the operator has a single mental model for both views; (3) **state persistence** — filters (query / authors / prefixes) survive reloads via `ecom-ops:git-log:filters:v1` localStorage, so a focused "what changed in the last 50 commits by `hermesagent`?" view stays sticky.
- **Feature class:** live-data-integration + interactive-tool + state-persistence (3-in-1, one bounded tick)
- **What shipped:** (a) `dashboard/scripts/parse-content.mjs` — new `parseGitLog()` that shells out to `git -C <root> log --pretty=format:<HASH>%n<SHORT>%n<DATE>%n<AUTHOR>%n<SUBJECT>%n--END-SUBJECT--%n<BODY>%n--END-COMMIT--> -- dashboard/ docs/journal.md` and parses the result into an array of `{sha, date, author, subject, body}` (capped at 200 commits, graceful failure → `[]` if git unavailable). (b) `dashboard/src/lib/content.ts` — new `GitCommit` interface + `gitCommits: GitCommit[]` field on the `Content` interface + `counts.gitCommits`. (c) `dashboard/src/components/git-change-log.tsx` — 290-line React component with: search input, conventional-commit prefix chips (feat/fix/chore/docs/refactor/perf/style/test/skill/journal), author chips, click-to-expand commit body, GitHub deep links on each SHA, copy-as-markdown for the filtered list, and a "show all N commits / collapse to 30" toggle. (d) `dashboard/app/journal/page.tsx` — wired `<GitChangeLog />` below the existing `<JournalSearch />` with a header paragraph explaining the two views.
- **Why a build-time capture (not a runtime API route):** the Vercel-side build only ships the dashboard subtree — no `.git` directory. A `/api/git-log` server route would always return "no commits". Capturing at build time means every cron tick re-bakes the log via `node scripts/parse-content.mjs`, so the data is always fresh on every deploy.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/journal — scroll past the JournalSearch timeline to see "Real change log" panel with 200 commit history.

## 2026-09-18 08:17 — Dashboard tick: keep — `TrajectoryScenarioComparator` adds Reset A / Reset B / Reset both (Move #128.an one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence)

- **Status:** keep
- **Reason:** Closes the comparator reset loop on the operator-UX side. The Move #128.al + Move #128.am comparator ships two persisted scenarios (A: always-on; B: toggled) stored in `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario:v1` + `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-b:v1` localStorage keys plus `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario:update` + `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-b:update` same-tab CustomEvents. Until now, an operator who wanted to dismiss a previously-chosen scenario had three ugly workarounds: (a) manually edit the dropdowns back to the default #1 + 30-day delay (clunky, easy to forget), (b) open DevTools → Application → Local Storage → delete both keys (technical, breaks other settings if misclicked), or (c) clear site data (catastrophic — wipes Your-store, shipped-playbooks, override, top10-shipped, and every other dashboard key). Move #128.an ships three one-click resets (Reset A / Reset B / Reset both) inside the comparator card, scoped to ONLY the comparator's two keys. Reset A removes the A key. Reset B rewrites the B key as `{enabled: false}` so the "Compare against a 2nd scenario" toggle un-checks automatically. Reset both shows a confirm() dialog before wiping (since it removes BOTH keys). All three reuse the comparator's existing event listeners, so the delta grid + status footer + move-picker dropdowns re-hydrate to defaults with zero extra wiring.
- **Feature class:** one-click-action + cross-page-intelligence (operator now resets Scenario A or Scenario B or both inside the comparator without touching DevTools; cross-tab `storage` event keeps `/` + `/today` dual-open cockpits in sync; the same-tab CustomEvent the comparator already listens for re-hydrates the originating card instantly)

SSR-safe via `typeof window === "undefined"` guard. Quota / private-mode silent fall-through. Reset-B additionally rewrites the B key with `{schema, version, enabled: false, state: {moveId: null, delayDays: 30}}` so the comparator's toggle un-checks automatically. ## 2026-09-19 18:53 — Dashboard tick: keep — Trajectory scenario presets library (Move #128.aq one-click-action + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence)

- **Status:** keep
- **Reason:** Closes the operator's "I tweak Scenario A, lose the previous tweak, tweak again, lose again" loop. The Move #128.al comparator persists ONE active Scenario A (and optional Scenario B) into `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario:v1` + `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-b:v1` localStorage keys, but until now there was no way to keep MORE THAN ONE saved scenario around — picking a new move in the dropdown overwrote the previous state. Move #128.aq ships a named-preset library that stores up to 12 presets in `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-presets:v1` with `{id, name, slot, moveId, delayDays, createdAt, updatedAt}`. The operator can Save (saves current comparator state as a named preset), Apply (one click restores a preset into the comparator's slot), Rename (inline input + Enter), and Delete (rose-accented ✕ with `window.confirm()` for destructive safety). Cap of 12 presets — beyond that, the helper refuses with `false` since the operator is doing portfolio work, not scenario what-if. Reuses the canonical storage-key + same-tab CustomEvent pattern (`ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-presets:update`) so a future rename in one module only needs a one-line edit in the other. Mirrors the visual style of Move #128.ao's export row (same border + muted background) so the dashboard's "scenario-controls" surfaces stay consistent.
- **Feature class:** one-click-action + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence (operator saves the current comparator state as a named preset, applies it back with one click, renames inline, or deletes with a confirm dialog — all cross-tab synced via `storage` event, same-tab synced via the new `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-presets:update` CustomEvent)
- **What shipped:** (a) `dashboard/src/lib/trajectory-scenario-presets.ts` — NEW (~310 LOC) — pure-logic helpers: `loadPresets`, `savePreset`, `applyPreset`, `deletePreset`, `renamePreset`, `countPresets`, `normalizePresetName`, `presetId`, `todayIso`, plus `PRESETS_STORAGE_KEY` + `PRESETS_EVENT` + `PRESETS_SCHEMA` + `PRESETS_VERSION` + `PRESETS_MAX` (12) constants. Schema is `{schema, version, presets: ScenarioPreset[]}`. SSR-safe via `typeof window === "undefined"` guards. Quota / private-mode silent fall-through. Save-on-existing-name replaces in place and returns `replaced: true`. Rename refuses collisions (case-insensitive within the same slot). (b) `dashboard/src/components/trajectory-scenario-presets-panel.tsx` — NEW (~430 LOC) — `TrajectoryScenarioPresetsPanel` client component with two modes: compact (chip row, mounted on both `/` and `/today`) and full (with name input + slot A/B toggle + save/apply/rename/delete buttons). Hydrates from localStorage on mount, subscribes to BOTH `storage` (cross-tab) AND `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-presets:update` (same-tab) AND the comparator's own `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario:update` + `ecom-ops:trajectory-scenario-b:update` events. Apply writes the chosen preset's slot via the canonical `STORAGE_KEY_A`/`STORAGE_KEY_B` + dispatches the comparator's same-tab CustomEvent so the comparator re-hydrates instantly. Each preset chip carries a slot badge (violet for A, sky for B), the name (max 160 px truncate + native tooltip), a `+30d` delay label, and 3 action buttons: Apply (border), ✎ Rename (border), ✕ Delete (rose accent). Until now an operator who built up a thoughtful presets library on their own browser had no way to share those presets with a teammate (or move them to a second browser) without copy-pasting move IDs by hand or rebuilding them from screenshots. Move #128.ar ships a one-click **Export → JSON file** + one-click **Import ← JSON file** round-trip so two operators can mirror a presets library in 5 seconds. The export shape is the canonical `{schema, version, presets: [...]}` payload, the import helper accepts three shapes (full storage payload, bare array, single preset), the merge defaults to additive (skips matching ids) with an optional `replaceExisting: true` flag for full-sync overwrites, and the helper enforces the canonical `PRESETS_MAX` (12) cap with skipped-counter surfacing. Status line shows "Imported N new preset(s) (M skipped)" so the operator always sees the merge result without opening DevTools.
